title: NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own) — Nullification from Inception
content:
Tidemark nullifies a policy under the NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own), voiding it from inception as if it had never been issued, for one of three reasons:

| Reason | Meaning |
|---|---|
| No insurable interest | the named insured never had an ownership or tenancy interest in the property |
| Ineligible property | the building is not insurable under the NFIP, such as a building entirely over water or in a non-participating or suspended community at issue |
| Premium payment dishonored | the application premium was dishonored |

**Decision and status.** Nullification is decided by Tidemark on its records, never on the customer's request, and is processed only on a policy whose status is pending effective or in force, which it leaves nullified.

**Effective date.** The cancellation effective date is the original effective date.

**Credits.** Every component collected on the policy, the Federal Policy Fee and probation surcharge included, is credited as a nullification credit and refunded to the payor of record; under a dishonored premium payment nothing was collected, so no credit or refund is booked.

**Claims.** A claim on a nullified policy is not payable.

## Points of judgement

- A customer asking for a policy to be "voided" does not by that request cause a nullification; the decision rests on Tidemark's records.
- A lapsed or cancelled policy is not nullified, because nullification is processed only on a pending-effective or in-force policy.
- Hypothetically, a policy nullified for no insurable interest after collecting a premium returns every collected component to the payor of record, fees included; one nullified for a dishonored premium returns nothing because nothing was collected.
